questions.question: Give a reason why petrol should not contain a high proportion of heptane.
questions.answer: Heptane is a straight-chain alkane with a low octane rating, so it causes knocking and poor engine performance.
steps: Petrol must burn smoothly in an engine, which needs a high octane rating.
Straight-chain alkanes such as heptane have a low octane rating.
A low octane fuel auto-ignites before the spark (knocking), reducing engine efficiency and causing damage.
Branched alkanes and cycloalkanes have higher octane ratings and are preferred in petrol.

questions.question: Draw the skeletal formula of 2,2,3-trimethylbutane.
questions.answer: A zigzag four-carbon butane chain with two methyl branches on C2 and one methyl branch on C3 (C7H16).
steps: Start with a butane backbone: four carbons in a zigzag line, numbered C1 to C4.
Add two methyl (CH3) groups to C2, so C2 has four bonds in total.
Add one methyl group to C3.
Check the formula: 7 carbons and 16 hydrogens, giving C7H16.

questions.question: Write the equation for reforming heptane into cycloheptane using molecular formulae.
steps: Heptane is C7H16, a straight-chain alkane.
Cycloheptane is a cycloalkane with formula CnH2n, so C7H14.
Reforming forms a ring by removing hydrogen, released as H2.

questions.question: Explain how oxides of nitrogen formed when petrol burns in an engine damage trees.
questions.answer: NOx dissolve in rain to form nitric acid (acid rain), which lowers soil pH, damages roots and leaves, and stops nutrient uptake.
steps: At high engine temperatures N2 and O2 from air react to form nitrogen monoxide, which is oxidised to NO2.
NO2 reacts with water and oxygen in the atmosphere to form nitric acid, HNO3.
The acid falls as acid rain and lowers the pH of soil.
Acidic soil damages roots and leaves and stops trees taking up nutrients.

questions.question: Name the first step in the mechanism Cl2 -> 2Cl.
questions.answer: Initiation (homolytic fission of the Cl-Cl bond).
steps: Cl2 contains a covalent Cl-Cl bond.
UV light supplies the energy needed to break this bond.
Homolytic fission splits the bond so each Cl atom takes one electron, forming two chlorine radicals.
This first step, which creates radicals, is the initiation step.

questions.question: Give the two propagation steps forming chloroheptane, using molecular formulae.
questions.answer: C7H16 + Cl -> C7H15 + HCl; then C7H15 + Cl2 -> C7H15Cl + Cl
steps: Propagation steps use a radical to make a new radical, so the chain continues.
Step 1: a Cl radical removes an H atom from heptane, giving HCl and a C7H15 radical.
Step 2: the C7H15 radical reacts with Cl2, giving chloroheptane C7H15Cl and a new Cl radical.
The new Cl radical returns to step 1, repeating the chain.

questions.question: Give the termination step which forms a hydrocarbon.
steps: Termination removes radicals by combining them, so no new radicals are formed.
Two heptyl radicals (C7H15) combine by forming a C-C bond.
The product C14H30 is a hydrocarbon with no chlorine.
This stops the chain reaction.

questions.question: Explain how dichloroheptane, C7H14Cl2, also forms during the reaction of heptane with chlorine.
questions.answer: Chloroheptane is attacked again by Cl radicals and Cl2: C7H15Cl + Cl -> C7H14Cl + HCl, then C7H14Cl + Cl2 -> C7H14Cl2 + Cl.
steps: Chloroheptane still has C-H bonds that a Cl radical can attack.
A Cl radical removes an H atom from C7H15Cl, forming HCl and a C7H14Cl radical.
This radical reacts with Cl2 to give C7H14Cl2 and regenerates a Cl radical.
Repeated substitution of H by Cl gives dichloroheptane.

questions.question: Which property do members of the alkane homologous series all share? A boiling temperature, B density, C empirical formula, D general formula.
steps: A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties.
Members differ by a CH2 unit, so their boiling temperatures and densities change down the series.
Their empirical formulae differ, for example ethane is CH3 and propane is C3H8 (empirical C3H8).
All alkanes share the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.question: Write the equation for reforming hexane into cyclohexane, using skeletal formulae.
questions.answer: Skeletal hexane (zigzag chain of six carbons) -> cyclohexane (six-membered ring) + H2; i.e. C6H14 -> C6H12 + H2
steps: Hexane is a straight chain of six carbons, C6H14.
Reforming joins C1 and C6 to form a six-membered ring, losing two H atoms.
Cyclohexane is a six-membered ring of carbons, C6H12.
The hydrogen released is H2: C6H14 -> C6H12 + H2.

questions.question: Give the name of cycloalkane D, whose skeletal formula is shown.
steps: D is a five-membered carbon ring (cyclopentane) with two CH3 groups attached.
The two methyl groups are on carbons separated by one ring carbon (the top vertex has no substituent), so they are on carbons 1 and 3.
Name: 1,3-dimethylcyclopentane.

questions.question: Give the molecular formula of cycloalkane D.
steps: The ring has 5 carbons and there are 2 methyl carbons, so 7 carbons in total.
It is a cycloalkane, so the formula is CnH2n: n = 7 gives C7H14.
Check by counting H: three ring CH2 (6 H) + two ring CH (2 H) + two CH3 (6 H) = 14 H.

questions.question: Complete the skeletal formulae of the other three structural isomers of C6H12 that have a four-carbon ring.
steps: All isomers have a four-carbon ring plus two more carbons as substituents: C4 ring + C2 = C6H12.
The first box shows two CH3 groups on adjacent ring carbons: 1,2-dimethylcyclobutane.
Box 2: a square with both CH3 groups on the same corner (two lines from one vertex): 1,1-dimethylcyclobutane.
Box 3: a square with one CH3 on each of two opposite corners: 1,3-dimethylcyclobutane.
Box 4: a square with a single two-carbon line (a bent line of two bonds) from one corner: ethylcyclobutane.

questions.question: Cycloalkane E has a molar mass of 126 g mol-1. Deduce its molecular formula.
steps: Cycloalkanes have the general formula CnH2n.
The molar mass of CnH2n is 12.0n + 2.0n = 14n.
Molecular formula C9H18; check: 108 + 18 = 126 g mol-1.

questions.question: 25 cm3 of gaseous cyclopentane is burned with 250 cm3 of oxygen (excess). Calculate the volume of each gas remaining, all at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.answer: O2 62.5 cm3; CO2 125 cm3; H2O (gas) 125 cm3
steps: From 2C5H10 + 15O2 -> 10CO2 + 10H2O, one volume of C5H10 needs 7.5 volumes of O2.
O2 needed for 25 cm3 C5H10 = 25 x 7.5 = 187.5 cm3.
O2 remaining = 250 - 187.5 = 62.5 cm3 (oxygen is in excess).
CO2 formed = 25 x 5 = 125 cm3 and H2O(g) formed = 25 x 5 = 125 cm3, since volume ratios equal mole ratios at the same T and P.

questions.question: Name the mechanism and type of reaction when cyclobutane reacts with chlorine in sunlight.
questions.answer: Free radical substitution, by a chain mechanism.
steps: Chlorine radicals are formed by light (initiation).
A radical attacks a C-H bond of cyclobutane, and a C-H bond is replaced by C-Cl.
The reaction proceeds by a chain of propagation steps.
Type: substitution, mechanism: free radical.

questions.question: Complete the equation for the initiation step of the reaction of cyclobutane with chlorine, including curly arrows.
questions.answer: Cl2 -> 2Cl (homolytic fission of the Cl-Cl bond; curly half-arrow from the bond to each Cl)
steps: Sunlight or UV provides the energy to break the Cl-Cl bond.
Homolytic fission: each Cl atom takes one electron from the bond.
Draw a curly half-arrow from the centre of the Cl-Cl bond to each Cl atom.
Products: two chlorine free radicals, Cl.

questions.question: Write the two propagation steps forming chlorocyclobutane, using C4H8 for cyclobutane.
questions.answer: C4H8 + Cl -> C4H7 + HCl; C4H7 + Cl2 -> C4H7Cl + Cl
steps: Step 1: a Cl radical abstracts an H atom from C4H8, giving HCl and a cyclobutyl radical C4H7.
Step 2: the C4H7 radical reacts with Cl2, giving chlorocyclobutane C4H7Cl and a new Cl radical.
The Cl radical formed in step 2 starts step 1 again.
Each propagation step keeps the chain going.

questions.question: Deduce the skeletal formula of the small amount of hydrocarbon formed in the reaction of cyclobutane with chlorine, and justify your answer.
questions.answer: Two cyclobutane rings joined by a single C-C bond (cyclobutylcyclobutane, C8H14), formed by combination of two cyclobutyl radicals.
steps: A hydrocarbon (no chlorine) is formed only by termination of two alkyl radicals.
The radical present is the cyclobutyl radical, C4H7.
Two C4H7 radicals join, giving C8H14.
Skeletal formula: two square rings linked by one bond.

questions.question: What is the total number of structural isomers with molecular formula C6H14? A 4, B 5, C 6, D 7.
steps: Structural isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are bonded.
Straight chain: hexane (1 isomer).
Methylpentanes: 2-methylpentane and 3-methylpentane (2 isomers).
Dimethylbutanes: 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane (2 isomers), giving a total of 5.

questions.question: Name molecule X, a halogen-containing compound that reacts with ozone in the upper atmosphere.
steps: The molecule has two carbons joined by a single bond (ethane): CH2Cl-CHCl2.
One carbon carries two Cl atoms and the other carbon carries one Cl.
Number so the Cl locants are as low as possible: 1,1,2.
Name: 1,1,2-trichloroethane, formula C2H3Cl3.

questions.question: State the essential condition necessary for homolytic fission of the C-Cl bond in the upper atmosphere.
steps: Homolytic fission of a C-Cl bond needs energy to break the covalent bond.
UV radiation supplies this energy in the upper atmosphere.
Each atom of the bond takes one electron, forming radicals.
So the essential condition is UV radiation.

questions.question: Write an equation for homolytic fission of the C-Cl bond in molecule X, including curly half-arrows.
questions.answer: CH2ClCHCl2 -> CH2ClCHCl + Cl (C-Cl bond breaks homolytically, one electron to each atom)
steps: Homolytic fission: the two electrons of the C-Cl bond are shared out one each, giving two radicals.
Draw X with a curly half-arrow (fish-hook, single barbed) from the middle of the C-Cl bond to the C atom, and a second half-arrow from the middle of the bond to the Cl atom.
Products: the organic radical CH2ClCHCl (C2H3Cl2) and a chlorine radical Cl.
Breaking a C-Cl bond in the CH2Cl group instead is equally valid and gives CHCl2CH2 + Cl.

questions.question: Write an equation for the reaction of a chlorine free radical with a molecule of X.
questions.answer: CH2ClCHCl2 + Cl -> CHClCHCl2 + HCl (i.e. C2H3Cl3 + Cl -> C2H2Cl3 + HCl)
steps: A Cl radical is very reactive and takes a hydrogen atom from X (a propagation step).
This forms hydrogen chloride and a new organic radical, C2H2Cl3.
Check: C 2 = 2; H 3 = 2 + 1; Cl 3 + 1 = 3 + 1 (one Cl in HCl).
Removing the H from CHCl2 instead gives CH2ClCCl2 + HCl, which is also acceptable.

questions.question: Write an equation, using displayed formulae, for a free radical formed in the sequence that gives a molecule with formula C4H4Cl6.
steps: C4H4Cl6 is two C2H2Cl3 radicals joined together: 2 x C2H2Cl3 = C4H4Cl6.
The radical formed in (b)(iii) is CHClCHCl2 (C2H2Cl3), with the unpaired electron on the carbon that lost an H.
Two of these radicals combine, forming a new C-C bond between the two radical carbons.
Displayed formula: each carbon shown with all its bonds; the product is Cl2CH-CHCl-CHCl-CHCl2 with all C-H and C-Cl bonds drawn.

questions.question: State the type of reaction occurring in (b)(iv) and name the product with formula C4H4Cl6.
steps: Two radicals combine and no radical remains, so the chain is ended: this is a termination step.
The product is a four-carbon chain: CHCl2-CHCl-CHCl-CHCl2.
Cl atoms are on carbons 1,1,2,3,4,4, so the name is 1,1,2,3,4,4-hexachlorobutane.
Check the formula: C4H4Cl6.

questions.question: What is the empirical formula of butane? A C4H10, B C2H5, C CH2.5, D CnH2n+2.
steps: The empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a formula.
Butane is C4H10; the ratio C:H is 4:10.
Dividing both by 2 gives 2:5, so C2H5.
CH2.5 is not a whole-number ratio and CnH2n+2 is a general formula.

questions.question: Give a reason why incomplete combustion of heptane sometimes occurs.
questions.answer: There is an insufficient (limited) supply of oxygen, so carbon forms CO or carbon instead of CO2.
steps: Complete combustion needs enough oxygen to oxidise all carbon to CO2.
If the air supply is limited, some carbon is only partly oxidised.
This forms carbon monoxide (CO) or carbon particulates (soot).
So incomplete combustion occurs when oxygen is in short supply.

questions.question: Write the equation for the incomplete combustion of heptane forming only carbon monoxide and water.
steps: Carbon: 7 C atoms in C7H16 give 7 CO.
Hydrogen: 16 H atoms give 8 H2O.
Oxygen on the right: 7 (from CO) + 8 (from H2O) = 15 O atoms, so 7.5 O2 are needed.
Doubling for whole numbers gives 2C7H16 + 15O2 -> 14CO + 16H2O.

questions.question: Draw skeletal formulae of a branched-chain alkane and a cycloalkane, each containing seven carbon atoms.
questions.answer: Branched alkane: 2-methylhexane (six-carbon chain with one CH3 on C2); cycloalkane: methylcyclohexane (six-carbon ring with one CH3 attached).
steps: Branched alkane: a chain of six carbons with a methyl group on C2 gives seven carbons, C7H16.
Cycloalkane: a six-membered ring with one methyl group attached gives seven carbons, C7H14.
Each skeletal line represents a C-C bond; carbons at corners are implied.
Both structures satisfy the alkane formula for their type.

questions.question: Write the equation for the reforming of heptane into a cycloalkane, using molecular formulae.
steps: Heptane is C7H16.
A cycloalkane with seven carbons is C7H14.
Reforming removes H2 as the ring forms.

questions.question: Give a reason for adding cycloalkanes to petrol.
questions.answer: Cycloalkanes have high octane ratings, which reduces knocking and improves engine performance.
steps: Petrol needs components with high octane ratings.
Cycloalkanes and branched alkanes burn more smoothly than straight-chain alkanes.
Smoother burning reduces knocking in the engine.
So cycloalkanes are added to improve the octane rating.

questions.question: State the type and mechanism of the reaction of heptane with chlorine in ultraviolet radiation.
questions.answer: Free radical substitution, by a chain (radical) mechanism.
steps: UV radiation starts the reaction by forming chlorine radicals.
Radicals attack C-H bonds in heptane, replacing H with Cl.
The reaction is a chain of propagation steps.
Type: substitution; mechanism: free radical.

questions.question: Give the mechanism for the reaction of heptane with chlorine giving C7H15Cl, C14H30 and HCl as the only products, naming each step.
questions.answer: Initiation: Cl2 -> 2Cl. Propagation: C7H16 + Cl -> C7H15 + HCl, then C7H15 + Cl2 -> C7H15Cl + Cl. Termination: C7H15 + C7H15 -> C14H30.
steps: Initiation (homolytic fission, UV): Cl2 -> 2Cl radicals.
Propagation step 1: Cl radical + C7H16 -> C7H15 radical + HCl.
Propagation step 2: C7H15 radical + Cl2 -> C7H15Cl + Cl radical.
The Cl radical from step 2 repeats propagation step 1, so the chain continues.
Termination: two C7H15 radicals combine, C7H15 + C7H15 -> C14H30.
Name each step: initiation, propagation (two steps), termination.

questions.question: Which is an overall equation for free radical substitution of cyclopentane with bromine? A C5H8 + Br2 -> C5H8Br2; B C5H10 + Br2 -> C5H10Br2; C C5H10 + Br2 -> C5H8Br2 + H2; D C5H10 + Br2 -> C5H9Br + HBr.
steps: Substitution replaces one H with one Br, and HBr is released.
Option A uses the wrong starting formula (C5H8) for cyclopentane.
Option B adds Br2 across all bonds with no HBr, which is not substitution.
Option C releases H2 instead of HBr, which is not a substitution product.

questions.question: Which statement is not correct about this reaction system? A only the initiation step involves homolytic fission; B only some bromine is converted to radicals in initiation; C propagation forms more product than termination; D further substitution is likely.
steps: Statement B is correct: only a small fraction of Br2 is split in initiation.
Statement C is correct: each termination removes radicals while many propagation cycles give product.
Statement D is correct: the bromoalkane still has C-H bonds that can be substituted again.
Statement A is wrong: in propagation, a Br2 bond is broken homolytically by a radical, so homolytic fission is not limited to initiation.

questions.question: Which free radical is least likely to form in a propagation step in this reaction system?
steps: Propagation step 1: Br + C5H10 -> C5H9 + HBr, so the cyclopentyl radical C5H9 (A) is formed.
Propagation step 2: C5H9 + Br2 -> C5H9Br + Br, so Br (B) is formed.
Further substitution can give C5H8Br (C) in later propagation steps, so it can form.
An H atom radical would need a C-H bond to break homolytically with nothing to stabilise it, so it is not formed in propagation. Answer D.

questions.question: Which alkane could be formed in a termination step in this reaction system?
questions.answer: C: two cyclopentane rings joined by a single C-C bond (C10H18)
steps: Termination joins two radicals; the only organic radical present is the cyclopentyl radical, C5H9.
Two C5H9 radicals bond together to give two cyclopentyl rings joined by a single C-C bond, C10H18 (option C).

A is a fused two-ring C8H14 and B is a spiro C9H16, so neither has the 10 carbons that two C5H9 radicals give; D is straight-chain decane, C10H22, which has too many hydrogens to come from two ring radicals.

questions.question: Which process occurs in the initiation step of the reaction of methane with excess chlorine in UV light?
questions.answer: C: homolytic fission of the Cl-Cl bond, with a curly half-arrow from the bond to each Cl atom, giving two chlorine radicals (Cl2 -> 2Cl).
steps: Initiation starts the chain by making radicals.
UV light supplies the energy to break the Cl-Cl bond.
The bond breaks homolytically, each Cl atom taking one electron; this is shown by two half-arrows starting at the Cl-Cl bond, one to each Cl (option C).
Result: two Cl radicals.

questions.question: Which of these molecules could not be formed in a termination step? A C2H6, B CH3Cl, C CH2Cl2, D HCl.
steps: Termination joins two radicals, so the product must contain the atoms of two radicals.
C2H6 forms from CH3 + CH3; CH3Cl from CH3 + Cl; CH2Cl2 from CH2Cl + Cl.
HCl needs an H radical, which is not present in termination.
HCl is formed in propagation steps, so it cannot form in termination.

questions.question: Explain how the first four ionisation energies of aluminium show that it is in Group 3.
questions.answer: There is a large jump between the 3rd (2750) and 4th (11 600) ionisation energies, so Al has 3 outer electrons and is in Group 3.
steps: The first three ionisation energies increase steadily (578, 1820, 2750 kJ mol-1): three electrons are removed from the outer shell.
The 4th ionisation energy is far larger (11 600, about 4 times the 3rd).
The 4th electron has to be removed from an inner shell, which is closer to the nucleus and less shielded, so it is held much more strongly.
Three electrons in the outer shell means the element is in Group 3.

questions.question: Explain the general increase in first ionisation energy from sodium to argon across Period 3.
questions.answer: Nuclear charge increases across the period while the outer electrons are in the same shell, so atomic radius falls and the electrons are held more strongly.
steps: Across Period 3 the number of protons increases, so nuclear charge increases.
Outer electrons are added to the same shell, so shielding changes little.
The atomic radius decreases, so the attraction between nucleus and outer electrons increases.
More energy is needed to remove an outer electron, so ionisation energy rises.

questions.question: Explain why the first ionisation energy of aluminium is less than that of magnesium.
questions.answer: The outer electron of Al is in a 3p orbital, which is higher in energy than the 3s orbital holding the outer electron of Mg, so it is removed more easily.
steps: Magnesium's outer electron is in the 3s sub-shell.
Aluminium's outer electron is in the 3p sub-shell, which is higher in energy.
The 3p electron is shielded by the 3s electrons and is held less tightly.
So less energy is needed to remove it, despite Al having more protons.

questions.question: Describe the bonding in aluminium metal.
questions.answer: Metallic bonding: a lattice of positive Al3+ ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, held together by electrostatic attraction.
steps: Each aluminium atom gives up its three outer electrons.
These electrons become delocalised and move throughout the metal.
The positive Al3+ ions form a regular lattice.
Strong electrostatic attraction between the ions and the delocalised electrons holds the metal together.

questions.question: Give two possible reasons why aluminium is used for overhead power cables.
questions.answer: Aluminium has a low density, so the cables are light, and it is a good electrical conductor.
steps: Low density means the cables are light and need less support.
Delocalised electrons allow aluminium to conduct electricity well.
It is ductile, so it can be drawn into wire.
A thin oxide layer also resists corrosion (any two valid reasons).

questions.question: Complete the equation for aluminium nanoparticles reacting with water to form aluminium oxide and hydrogen (no state symbols).
steps: Aluminium forms Al2O3, so 2 Al are needed on the left.
Oxygen: Al2O3 has 3 O, so 3 H2O are needed.
Hydrogen: 3 H2O gives 6 H, which forms 3 H2.
Check: 2 Al, 6 H, 3 O on each side.

questions.question: Give two possible reasons for producing hydrogen from aluminium rather than from fossil fuels.
questions.answer: Aluminium can be obtained from recycled cans, so the source is renewable and not limited like fossil fuels; the reaction gives no carbon dioxide.
steps: Fossil fuels are finite, while recycled aluminium cans are a renewable source.
Producing hydrogen from fossil fuels releases CO2 and other greenhouse gases.
Aluminium reacting with water produces hydrogen with no carbon dioxide.
Any two of these reasons give full marks.

questions.question: When C20H42 is cracked, each molecule gives one ethene, one butane and two molecules of hydrocarbon E. What is the molecular formula of E? A C7H13, B C7H14, C C14H26, D C14H28.
steps: Carbon: 20 - 2 (ethene) - 4 (butane) = 14 C atoms for two E molecules, so 7 C each.
Hydrogen: 42 - 4 (ethene) - 10 (butane) = 28 H atoms for two E molecules, so 14 H each.
E is C7H14.
Check: C2H4 + C4H10 + 2C7H14 = C20H42.

questions.question: Petrol, bioethanol and hydrogen are fuels. All three of these fuels: A burn to produce greenhouse gases; B are overall carbon neutral; C are overall sustainable; D biodegrade rapidly.
questions.answer: A: burn to produce greenhouse gases
steps: Petrol and bioethanol burn to form carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) and water.
Hydrogen burns to form only water, and water vapour is also a greenhouse gas, so all three produce a greenhouse gas.
B is wrong: petrol is not carbon neutral. C is wrong: petrol is finite, so not sustainable.
D is wrong: hydrogen is a gas and petrol is not rapidly biodegradable.

questions.question: How many structural isomers have the formula C3H6Cl2? A 2, B 3, C 4, D 5.
steps: Structural isomers have the same formula with different connectivity.
The isomers are 1,1-dichloropropane, 1,2-dichloropropane, 1,3-dichloropropane and 2,2-dichloropropane.
Each isomer places the two Cl atoms on different carbon positions of propane.
Total: 4 structural isomers.

questions.question: All alkanes have the same: A empirical formula, B general formula, C molecular formula, D structural formula.
steps: Alkanes form a homologous series with a shared general formula, CnH2n+2.
Empirical formulae differ, for example C2H6 and C3H8 have different ratios.
Molecular and structural formulae differ between members of the series.
So only the general formula is common to all alkanes.

questions.question: Which atmospheric pollutant is not emitted during the combustion of alkane car fuels? A ammonia, B nitrogen dioxide, C sulfur dioxide, D octane.
steps: Car engines produce nitrogen oxides (NO and NO2) from N2 and O2 at high temperature.
Sulfur dioxide forms from sulfur impurities in the fuel.
Ammonia is not formed by combustion of alkanes or by the reaction of air in the engine.
Octane is a fuel component, not a pollutant, so the pollutant that is not emitted is ammonia.

questions.question: A single molecule of decane, C10H22, is cracked. Which mixture could not be formed? A pentene and pentane; B ethene, butene and butane; C propene, propane and butene; D hexene and propane.
steps: A: C5H10 + C5H12 = C10H22, possible.
B: C2H4 + C4H8 + C4H10 = C10H22, possible.
C: C3H6 + C3H8 + C4H8 = C10H22, possible.
D: C6H12 + C3H8 = C9H20, which does not balance C10H22, so it cannot form.

questions.question: When carrying out chemical experiments, for a given chemical: A the hazard is fixed but the risk varies; B the hazard varies but the risk is fixed; C both hazard and risk are fixed; D both hazard and risk vary.
steps: A hazard is a property of a substance that could cause harm, such as flammability.
The hazard of a given chemical does not change.
A risk is the likelihood of harm, which depends on how and how much the chemical is used.
So the hazard is fixed while the risk varies.

questions.question: A 0.210 g sample of volatile liquid C gives 72.5 cm3 of gas at 100 kPa and 358 K. Calculate the molar mass of C (pV = nRT, R = 8.31 J mol-1 K-1).
steps: Convert units: V = 72.5 cm3 = 7.25 x 10^-5 m3; p = 100 kPa = 1.00 x 10^5 Pa; T = 358 K.
Molar mass M = mass/moles = 0.210 g / 2.437 x 10^-3 mol.

questions.question: Using the molar mass from (a), give a possible name or formula for hydrocarbon C.
questions.answer: C6H14 (hexane or another C6H14 isomer; M = 86.0 g mol-1)
steps: C is a hydrocarbon with M of about 86 g mol-1.
C6H14: 6 x 12.0 + 14 x 1.0 = 86.0 g mol-1, which matches.
C6H12 (an alkene or cycloalkane) has M = 84.0 g mol-1, which does not match.
So C is hexane, C6H14, or one of its isomers.

questions.question: Ethane reacts with bromine in UV radiation. Which is the equation? A C2H6 + Br2 -> C2H4Br2 + H2; B C2H6 + Br2 -> C2H5Br + HBr; C C2H6 + Br2 -> 2CH3Br; D C2H6 + Br2 -> CH4 + CH2Br2.
steps: Free radical substitution replaces one H of ethane with Br, releasing HBr.
Option B shows exactly this: C2H5Br and HBr.
Option A releases H2, which is not a substitution product.
Options C and D involve breaking the C-C bond, which does not happen in this substitution.

questions.question: The ultraviolet radiation is needed for: A homolytic breaking of a Br-Br bond; B heterolytic breaking of a Br-Br bond; C homolytic breaking of a C-H bond; D heterolytic breaking of a C-H bond.
questions.answer: A (homolytic breaking of a Br-Br bond)
steps: UV radiation supplies energy for initiation.
Initiation splits Br2 into two Br radicals.
Splitting gives radicals, so the fission is homolytic (one electron to each atom).
C-H bonds are not broken in initiation, so option A is correct.

questions.question: Which of these occurs in a propagation step in the reaction of methane with chlorine?
questions.answer: B: CH3 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + Cl (radical attacks the Cl-Cl bond)
steps: A propagation step has a radical reacting with a molecule to give a product molecule and a new radical.
B shows the methyl radical forming a bond to one Cl of Cl2 while the Cl-Cl bond breaks, so CH3Cl and a Cl radical form.

A shows two radicals joining (termination). C and D do not give the products of the chlorination chain: C is a methyl radical attacking methane, and D breaks the C-H bond and Cl-Cl bond in one step without a radical reacting.

questions.question: Which pollutant cannot form when alkane fuels are burned in car engines? A hydrogen chloride, B sulfur dioxide, C carbon particulates, D carbon monoxide.
steps: Alkane fuels contain only carbon and hydrogen; they contain no chlorine.
Sulfur dioxide forms from sulfur impurities in the fuel.
Incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and carbon particulates (soot).
Without chlorine in the fuel, hydrogen chloride cannot form.

questions.question: What is the most significant hazard associated with the pollutant CO(g)? A major contributor to acid rain; B strongly absorbs infrared radiation; C toxic at low concentrations; D main cause of ozone depletion.
steps: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen does.
This reduces the amount of oxygen carried in the blood.
CO is toxic even at low concentrations and has no smell or colour.
Options A, B and D describe other gases (acid rain, greenhouse effect, ozone depletion), not the main hazard of CO.

questions.question: 40 cm3 of butane and 20 cm3 of oxygen react in a sealed system to form CO and H2 (C4H10 + 2O2 -> 4CO + 5H2). What is the total gas volume at the end, in cm3? A 30, B 60, C 90, D 120.
steps: Oxygen is limiting: each butane needs 2 O2, so 20 cm3 O2 reacts with 10 cm3 butane.
Products from 10 cm3 butane: 40 cm3 CO (4 x 10) and 50 cm3 H2 (5 x 10).
Unreacted butane = 40 - 10 = 30 cm3.
Total gas = 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 cm3.

questions.question: Which is not a step in the reaction of chlorine with propane in ultraviolet radiation?
steps: A: C3H7 + Cl -> C3H7Cl is a termination step.
B: C3H7 + C3H7 -> C6H14 is a termination step.
C: C3H7 + Cl2 -> C3H7Cl + Cl is a propagation step.
D would need a C3H7 radical to react with HCl and release H, which is not a step of the mechanism and would not form a stable hydrogen atom radical, so D is not a step.

questions.question: Give the molecular formula and IUPAC name for compound X, whose structure is shown and which is present in petrol.
steps: The longest chain is five carbons (pentane): one end carbon is quaternary and carries two methyl groups, and another chain carbon carries one methyl.
Numbering from the end nearer to the branches puts the methyl groups on C2, C2 and C4, so the name is 2,2,4-trimethylpentane.
Carbons: 5 + 3 = 8; for an alkane CnH2n+2 this is C8H18.

questions.question: Name the industrial process used to produce compound X from its straight-chain isomer.
steps: A straight-chain alkane is converted into a branched isomer of the same formula.
Isomerisation uses a catalyst and heat.
Branched alkanes have higher octane ratings, which is why the process is used for petrol.
The process type is isomerisation.

questions.question: Write an equation for the complete combustion of heptane, including state symbols.
steps: Complete combustion gives CO2 and H2O only.
Carbon: 7 C gives 7 CO2.
Hydrogen: 16 H gives 8 H2O; oxygen on the right = 14 + 8 = 22 O atoms, so 11 O2.
Heptane is a liquid at room temperature and water is liquid, so (l) for both; CO2 is (g) and O2 is (g).

questions.question: Identify, by name or formula, a pollutant that may result from incomplete combustion of heptane.
steps: Incomplete combustion occurs when oxygen is limited.
Carbon is then only partly oxidised, forming carbon monoxide.
Some carbon also forms soot, which is carbon particulates.
Either CO or carbon particulates is a valid answer.

questions.question: Give two environmental benefits of using electric cars, and justify each answer.
questions.answer: No CO2 (greenhouse gas) is emitted at the car, and no NOx, SO2 or particulates are emitted, reducing acid rain and smog.
steps: Electric cars do not burn fuel, so they emit no CO2 at the point of use.
This reduces the greenhouse effect and global warming (if the electricity is low-carbon).
Electric cars emit no NOx, SO2 or particulates from the exhaust.
This reduces acid rain and urban air pollution.

questions.question: What is the number of structural isomers with molecular formula C5H12? A six, B five, C four, D three.
steps: Structural isomers have the same formula with different carbon skeletons.
Straight chain: pentane.
One methyl branch: 2-methylbutane.
Two methyl branches on one carbon: 2,2-dimethylpropane. Total = 3.

questions.question: The reaction of methane with chlorine is a free radical substitution. Which termination step does not occur?
steps: Termination steps join two radicals that are present in the reaction mixture, here CH3 and Cl.
A (CH3 + CH3 -> C2H6), B (CH3 + Cl -> CH3Cl) and D (Cl + Cl -> Cl2) all use radicals formed in the chain mechanism.
H atoms (radicals) are not formed in the mechanism, so CH3 + H -> CH4 does not occur.

questions.question: Explain how the structure and bonding in graphite make it suitable for use as an electrode in the extraction of aluminium (refer to the diagram).
questions.answer: Graphite has layers of covalently bonded carbon atoms with delocalised electrons that conduct electricity, and its high melting point means it withstands the 950 deg C electrolysis.
steps: Each carbon is covalently bonded to three others in hexagonal layers, forming strong bonds.
Each carbon has one delocalised electron, which moves along the layers.
The delocalised electrons carry the current, so graphite conducts electricity.
The high melting point (giant covalent layers) means it does not melt at 950 deg C.

questions.question: Calculate the maximum volume of CO2 at r.t.p. produced when 1.00 kg of aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of Al2O3, where the oxygen produced reacts with the graphite electrode (molar volume 24.0 dm3 mol-1).
steps: Moles of Al = 1000 g / 27.0 g mol-1 = 37.0 mol.
Each Al needs 3 electrons; each O2 released at the anode gives 4 electrons, so 4 Al produce 3 O2.
The O2 reacts with graphite: C + O2 -> CO2, so 4 Al give 3 CO2 (overall 2Al2O3 + 3C -> 4Al + 3CO2).

questions.question: Suggest three ways that recycling about 7.2 billion aluminium cans per year reduces energy consumption.
questions.answer: Avoids the energy-intensive electrolysis of Al2O3 (at about 950 deg C); avoids mining and transporting bauxite; melting scrap needs much less energy than extraction.
steps: Extracting aluminium from Al2O3 by electrolysis uses very large amounts of electrical energy.
Recycling avoids this electrolysis step, which is the main energy cost.
Recycling avoids mining and transporting bauxite, saving the energy used for those.
Melting scrap aluminium needs much less energy than extracting it from ore.

questions.question: Why does free radical substitution have limited use in industrial chemistry? A reactions only occur in the upper atmosphere; B initiation requires UV radiation; C further substitution products are formed; D termination reactions produce unwanted products.
steps: Free radical substitution gives a mixture of products.
The product still has C-H bonds, which react further with chlorine or bromine.
This makes it hard to obtain a single pure product in good yield.
Options A and B are not true or not limiting, and D is minor.

questions.question: Suggest one difference between the fractional distillation of air and of crude oil.
questions.answer: Air is cooled until it liquefies and gases are separated by boiling points; crude oil is heated and vaporised, and separated into hydrocarbon fractions.
steps: Air is separated by cooling it to liquid air and fractionating the gases.
Crude oil is separated by heating it so that the hydrocarbons vaporise.
Crude oil separates into fractions of hydrocarbon chains of similar length.
Any one valid difference gains the mark.

questions.question: Dry air contains 21.0% oxygen by volume. Calculate the volume of air, in dm3, that must pass over zeolite to obtain 500 cm3 of gas containing 90% oxygen by volume (zeolite adsorbs nitrogen).
steps: Oxygen in the product: 90% of 500 cm3 = 450 cm3.
Zeolite removes nitrogen, so all the oxygen in the air passes through.

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of the bonding in a nitrogen molecule, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: N triple bond N: three shared pairs of electrons between the two N atoms, with one lone pair on each N atom (10 outer electrons).
steps: Each nitrogen atom has 5 outer electrons.
Three electrons from each N form three shared pairs, a triple covalent bond.
The remaining two electrons on each N form one lone pair.
Total outer electrons shown: 6 shared + 4 lone = 10.

questions.question: Liquid oxygen has density 1140 g dm-3. Calculate the volume in m3 of gas at r.t.p. obtained from a bottle containing 13.9 dm3 of liquid oxygen (molar volume 24.0 dm3 mol-1).
steps: Mass of liquid oxygen = 1140 g dm-3 x 13.9 dm3 = 15 850 g (15 846 g).
Moles of O2 = 15 846 g / 32.0 g mol-1 = 495.2 mol.
Volume of gas = 495.2 mol x 24.0 dm3 mol-1 = 11 885 dm3.

questions.question: The full bottle has a total mass of 80.0 kg. Calculate the mass of the empty bottle, using the working from (c)(i), to an appropriate number of significant figures.
steps: Mass of oxygen in the bottle = 15.846 kg from (c)(i).
Mass of empty bottle = 80.0 kg - 15.846 kg = 64.154 kg.
The total mass 80.0 kg has 3 significant figures, so give 3 s.f.
Answer: 64.2 kg.

questions.question: Explain why the container needs to have such a large mass.
questions.answer: The walls must be thick and strong to withstand the high pressure of the stored oxygen and to insulate the liquid oxygen, which is kept very cold.
steps: The container holds a large quantity of oxygen at high pressure.
Thick, strong walls are needed so the container does not rupture.
The liquid oxygen is stored at very low temperature, so the walls are insulated.
This extra material adds mass.

questions.question: Calculate the mean energy density, in MJ kg-1, of an E10 fuel containing 92.2% hydrocarbons and 7.80% ethanol by mass, using the energy densities of the two components shown.
steps: Take 1 kg of fuel: 0.922 kg hydrocarbons and 0.0780 kg ethanol.
Energy from hydrocarbons = 0.922 x 46.5 = 42.87 MJ.
Energy from ethanol = 0.0780 x 29.7 = 2.317 MJ.
Total = 45.19 MJ per kg, so the mean energy density = 45.2 MJ kg-1 (3 significant figures, the same as the data).

questions.question: The density of E10 fuel is 0.729 g cm-3. Calculate the mass of 1500 cm3 of the fuel.
steps: Mass = density x volume.
To 3 significant figures: 1090 g.
Answer: 1.09 x 10^3 g, or 1.09 kg.

questions.question: Calculate the energy released when 1500 cm3 of E10 fuel is burned in excess oxygen, using the answers from (a)(i) and (a)(ii). If (a)(i) was not calculated, use 38.1 MJ kg-1.
questions.answer: About 49.4 MJ using the mean energy density 45.2 MJ kg-1 from (a)(i) (41.7 MJ if the given 38.1 MJ kg-1 is used)
steps: Mass of fuel burned = 1500 cm3 x 0.729 g cm-3 = 1093.5 g = 1.0935 kg (from (a)(ii)).
Use the mean energy density from (a)(i): 45.2 MJ kg-1.
Energy = 1.0935 kg x 45.2 MJ kg-1 = 49.4 MJ.
If (a)(i) was not calculated, use 38.1 MJ kg-1: 1.0935 x 38.1 = 41.7 MJ.

questions.question: Explain how replacing E5 fuel with E10 fuel might result in a more sustainable fuel.
questions.answer: Ethanol is made from renewable plant material, so less crude oil is used; the CO2 released is taken in by plants as they grow, so overall CO2 emissions are lower.
steps: E10 contains more ethanol than E5, so a greater proportion of the fuel is renewable.
Ethanol comes from plant material (fermented sugars), which is renewable.
Less crude oil is used, which is a finite resource.
The CO2 released on burning ethanol is taken up by plants as they grow, so the net CO2 is lower (carbon neutral).

questions.question: Write the equation, using molecular formulae, for the reforming of hexane into a cyclic hydrocarbon with a five-carbon ring and hydrogen as the only products.
steps: Hexane is C6H14.
The cyclic product has a five-carbon ring with one CH3 group, which is methylcyclopentane, C6H12.
Reforming releases H2 as the ring forms.

questions.question: Draw the structure of the cyclic hydrocarbon formed in (c)(i).
questions.answer: Methylcyclopentane: a skeletal five-membered ring with one CH3 group attached to one ring carbon.
steps: The product has a ring of five carbon atoms.
The sixth carbon from hexane is a methyl (CH3) group attached to the ring.
Draw a pentagon with one line leaving it to represent the methyl group.
Formula check: C6H12.

questions.question: Describe the role of ultraviolet light in the initiation step of the reaction of hexane with chlorine.
questions.answer: UV light provides the energy to break the Cl-Cl bond by homolytic fission, forming chlorine radicals that start the chain reaction.
steps: UV light is absorbed by Cl2 molecules.
The energy absorbed is enough to break the Cl-Cl bond.
The bond breaks homolytically, giving two Cl radicals.
These radicals start the chain of propagation steps.

questions.question: Write equations for the propagation step and the termination step forming dodecane, C12H26, using molecular formulae.
questions.answer: Propagation: C6H14 + Cl -> C6H13 + HCl; Termination: 2C6H13 -> C12H26
steps: Propagation: a Cl radical removes H from hexane, forming a hexyl radical C6H13 and HCl.
Check propagation: C 6 = 6; H 14 = 13 + 1; Cl balanced.
Termination: two hexyl radicals combine to form C12H26.
Check termination: C 12 = 12; H 26 = 26.

questions.question: Draw the displayed formulae of the three alkanes with molecular formula C5H12.
steps: Pentane: five carbons in a straight chain, with each carbon bonded to the required H atoms.
2-methylbutane: four carbons in a chain with a CH3 on the second carbon.
2,2-dimethylpropane: a central carbon bonded to four CH3 groups.
Each structure has 12 H atoms and 5 C atoms.

questions.question: Give the systematic name of compound P, whose structure is shown.
steps: The longest carbon chain has six carbons (from the left end through the ethyl branch), so the parent is hexane.
There is a methyl on the second carbon (from the left) and a methyl on the fourth carbon, so the locants are 2 and 4 (numbering from the other end would give 3 and 5).
Name: 2,4-dimethylhexane (C8H18).

questions.question: The table shows boiling temperatures of the first four straight-chain alkanes. Predict the molecular formula and boiling temperature of the straight-chain alkane with five carbon atoms.
questions.answer: C5H12; boiling temperature about 36 deg C (accept roughly 30 to 40 deg C)
steps: The straight-chain alkane with five carbons is pentane, C5H12.
Boiling temperature rises with each CH2 added, but by smaller steps: +75, +47 and +41.5 deg C.
The next step is predicted to be about +37 deg C, so the estimate is -0.5 + 37 = about 36 deg C.
This fits the trend of stronger London forces as chain length increases.

questions.question: Write the equation for the incomplete combustion of propane, C3H8, forming carbon, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and water (no state symbols).
steps: Start with 2C3H8 to give whole numbers: 6 C and 16 H atoms.
Hydrogen: 16 H gives 8 H2O.
Carbon: 2 C + 2 CO + 2 CO2 uses 6 C atoms.
Oxygen: 2 CO (2) + 2 CO2 (4) + 8 H2O (8) = 14 O atoms, so 7 O2.

questions.question: Explain the toxicity of carbon monoxide.
questions.answer: CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than O2, forming carboxyhaemoglobin, so less oxygen is carried in the blood.
steps: Carbon monoxide is produced by incomplete combustion.
It binds to the haemoglobin in red blood cells.
It binds more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin.
Less oxygen is transported to tissues, which can cause headaches, unconsciousness or death.

questions.question: Write the two propagating steps showing how C3H7Cl is formed in the reaction of propane with chlorine (curly arrows not required).
questions.answer: C3H8 + Cl -> C3H7 + HCl; C3H7 + Cl2 -> C3H7Cl + Cl
steps: Step 1: a Cl radical removes an H atom from propane, forming C3H7 and HCl.
Step 2: the C3H7 radical reacts with Cl2, forming C3H7Cl and a new Cl radical.
The new Cl radical repeats step 1.
Check: C 3 = 3; H 8 = 7 + 1 in step 1.

questions.question: Identify the different C3H7Cl molecules produced in this reaction.
steps: Chlorine can replace a hydrogen on either end carbon or the middle carbon of propane.
Replacing H on an end carbon gives 1-chloropropane.
Replacing H on the middle carbon gives 2-chloropropane.
Both have the formula C3H7Cl.

questions.question: Give a reason why a mixture of C3H7Cl molecules is formed.
questions.answer: Propane has two different types of hydrogen (on CH3 and on CH2 groups), and a chlorine radical can attack either.
steps: Propane has primary H atoms on the two CH3 groups and secondary H atoms on the CH2 group.
A chlorine radical can remove either type of H atom.
Removing different H atoms gives different C3H7 radicals, and so different products.
So a mixture of isomeric C3H7Cl is formed.

questions.question: Give a reason why some hexane is formed in this reaction.
questions.answer: Two propyl radicals (C3H7) combine in a termination step: C3H7 + C3H7 -> C6H14.
steps: Termination combines two radicals to remove them from the chain.
Two C3H7 radicals are present in the reaction mixture.
They combine to form a C-C bond, giving C6H14.
So hexane is a termination product.

questions.question: A small amount of a product with molar mass 113 g mol-1 is formed. Deduce the structure and name of a possible product.
steps: Molar mass 113 corresponds to C3H6Cl2: 36.0 + 6.0 + 71.0 = 113.
This is propane with two H atoms replaced by Cl (a dichloropropane).
Example structure: CH3-CHCl-CH2Cl.
Name: 1,2-dichloropropane (other isomers such as 1,1- or 1,3-dichloropropane are also valid).

questions.question: Which of these fuels is obtained from fermented sugar cane? A ethanol, B hydrogen, C petrol, D propane.
steps: Fermentation of sugars from sugar cane by yeast produces ethanol.
Ethanol is a biofuel and is renewable.
Hydrogen, petrol and propane are not made by fermentation.
So the answer is ethanol.

questions.question: How many structural isomers have the formula C6H14? A 3, B 4, C 5, D 6.
steps: Straight chain: hexane.
Methylpentanes: 2-methylpentane and 3-methylpentane.
Dimethylbutanes: 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

questions.question: Which substances are formed from the combustion of petrol in car engines? A water, carbon dioxide and hydrogen; B water, carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride; C water, carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide; D water, carbon particulates and hydrogen.
questions.answer: C (water, carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide)
steps: Combustion of hydrocarbons gives water and carbon dioxide.
Sulfur impurities in petrol are oxidised to sulfur dioxide.
Hydrogen and hydrogen chloride are not formed in combustion of petrol.
So option C is correct.

questions.question: Which mixture could be formed when a single molecule of C12H26 is cracked? A butene, pentane and propene; B hexane, butene and ethane; C nonane and ethene; D propene and decane.
steps: A: C4H8 + C5H12 + C3H6 gives C12 and H (8 + 12 + 6) = 26, so C12H26.
B: C6H14 + C4H8 + C2H6 gives H 28, which does not balance.
C: C9H20 + C2H4 gives C11H24, which does not balance.
D: C3H6 + C10H22 gives C13H28, which does not balance.

questions.question: Give the molecular formula, empirical formula and IUPAC name of isooctane, which has eight carbon atoms and the skeletal formula shown.
questions.answer: Molecular formula C8H18; empirical formula C4H9; IUPAC name 2,2,4-trimethylpentane.
steps: Isooctane is a saturated alkane with 8 carbons, so C8H18 (general formula CnH2n+2).
Empirical formula: divide 8:18 by 2 to give 4:9, so C4H9.
Isooctane is the branched isomer 2,2,4-trimethylpentane: a pentane chain with two methyl groups on C2 and one on C4.
Check the carbons: 5 in the chain + 3 methyl groups = 8.

questions.question: Name the technique used to separate isooctane from octane in a laboratory, based on their boiling temperatures.
steps: The two isomers have different boiling temperatures (99 deg C and 125 deg C).
The technique that separates liquids by boiling point is distillation.
The same technique is used for crude oil.
Use a fractionating column for a clean separation: fractional distillation.

questions.question: Describe how fractional distillation separates isooctane from octane.
questions.answer: The mixture is heated and vapour rises up a fractionating column; isooctane (lower boiling temperature) condenses and is collected first, while octane condenses lower down the column.
steps: The mixture is heated, and vapour enters the fractionating column.
The column is hotter at the bottom and cooler at the top.
Repeated vaporisation and condensation enriches the vapour in the lower-boiling isooctane.
Isooctane (99 deg C) reaches the top and is collected first; octane (125 deg C) stays lower in the column.

questions.question: Write the equation for the complete combustion of isooctane (state symbols not required).
steps: Complete combustion gives CO2 and H2O.
Carbon: 8 C gives 8 CO2.
Hydrogen: 18 H gives 9 H2O.
Oxygen on the right: 16 + 9 = 25 O atoms, so 12.5 O2.

questions.question: Describe how carbon monoxide and nitrogen monoxide are formed in car engines, including the conditions required (equations may be included).
questions.answer: CO forms from incomplete combustion when oxygen is limited, e.g. C8H18 + 8.5O2 -> 8CO + 9H2O; NO forms when N2 and O2 from air react at the high temperature of the engine: N2 + O2 -> 2NO.
steps: CO forms when there is insufficient oxygen (a fuel-rich mixture), so carbon is only partly oxidised.
Example: C8H18 + 8.5O2 -> 8CO + 9H2O.
NO forms when N2 and O2 from the air react at the high temperature and pressure in the engine cylinder.
Equation: N2 + O2 -> 2NO; high temperature is needed to break the strong N-N triple bond.

questions.question: Identify another pollutant, other than carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and nitrogen monoxide, produced in car engines.
questions.answer: Sulfur dioxide (SO2), from sulfur impurities in the fuel (unburnt hydrocarbons or carbon particulates are also valid).
steps: Petrol contains small amounts of sulfur compounds.
On combustion these form sulfur dioxide, SO2.
SO2 causes acid rain.
Any one valid pollutant, such as unburnt hydrocarbons or particulates, gains the mark.

questions.question: State the type and mechanism of the reaction of isooctane with excess chlorine.
steps: Chlorine radicals, formed by UV light, attack C-H bonds in isooctane.
A C-H bond is replaced by C-Cl, giving chlorinated products.
The reaction proceeds through a chain of propagation steps.
Type: substitution; mechanism: free radical.

questions.question: Give the essential condition required for the reaction of isooctane with chlorine.
steps: UV light provides the energy to break the Cl-Cl bond.
This homolytic fission forms chlorine radicals.
The radicals start the free radical chain reaction.
Without UV light, the reaction does not start readily.

questions.question: One chlorinated compound contains 44.1% carbon and 6.9% hydrogen by mass. Calculate its molecular formula.
steps: Percentage of Cl = 100 - 44.1 - 6.9 = 49.0%.
Divide by 1.380: C 2.66; H 5.00; Cl 1.00. Multiply by 3: C 8 : H 15 : Cl 3.
Formula C8H15Cl3 (M = 217.5 g mol-1), consistent with 44.1% C and 6.9% H.

questions.question: What is the best definition of a hydrocarbon? A a compound containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen; B a compound containing carbon and hydrogen only; C a compound that contains single carbon to carbon bonds; D a mixture containing carbon and hydrogen only.
questions.answer: B (a compound containing carbon and hydrogen only)
steps: A hydrocarbon is an organic compound made only of carbon and hydrogen.
Option A includes oxygen, so it is not a hydrocarbon.
Option C describes alkanes only, not all hydrocarbons.
Option D describes a mixture, and a hydrocarbon is a single compound.

questions.question: Three isomeric cycloalkanes X, Y and Z are shown. Which react with chlorine to produce four different monochlorinated products? A all 3; B X and Z only; C Y and Z only; D X only.
questions.answer: B: Isomer X and Isomer Z only
steps: Count the different hydrogen environments, since each gives one monochloro product.
X is methylcyclobutane: CH3, the ring CH, the two equivalent CH2 next to it, and the CH2 opposite it give 4 products.
Y is 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane: the six CH3 hydrogens are equivalent and the two ring CH2 are equivalent, so only 2 products.
Z is ethylcyclopropane: CH3, CH2, ring CH and the ring CH2 (two equivalent carbons) give 4 products.
So X and Z only, option B.

questions.question: Polymerisation of alkenes is started by a peroxide, R-O-O-R. Which step in the mechanism is an initiation step?
steps: Initiation is the first step, which forms free radicals from a non-radical molecule.
In A the weak O-O bond of the peroxide breaks homolytically to give two R-O radicals.
B and C are a propagation step and a termination step; D is also propagation, as a radical reacts with an alkene to start building the chain.
So A is the initiation step.

questions.question: Which statement about the cracking of crude oil is true? A separates the mixture into pure compounds; B separates the mixture into fractions; C separates saturated from unsaturated compounds; D decreases the average number of carbon atoms per molecule.
steps: Cracking breaks long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful molecules.
Shorter molecules have fewer carbon atoms, so the average falls.
Separation into fractions is done by fractional distillation, not cracking (option B).
So option D is correct.

questions.question: Which structures represent a pair of isomers?
steps: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structures, so count the carbons in each skeleton.
A: the left structure is 2-methylpentane (6 C) and the right is 2,3-dimethylbutane (6 C), so both are C6H14 with different structures: isomers.
B: pentane (5 C) and 2,3-dimethylbutane (6 C) differ in formula. C: 2-methylbutane (5 C) and a 6-carbon alkane differ in formula.
D: 2-methylbutane (C5H12) and 2-methylpropane (C4H10) differ in formula. So the answer is A.

questions.question: Name the type and mechanism of the reaction between halogens and alkanes.
steps: Halogens replace hydrogen atoms in alkanes, which is substitution.
The reaction is started by UV light, forming halogen radicals.
Radicals attack alkane C-H bonds in a chain of steps.
Mechanism: free radical.

questions.question: Give the equation for the initiation step when chlorine reacts with butane, including arrows and electrons.
questions.answer: Cl-Cl -> 2Cl (homolytic fission; a curly half-arrow from the Cl-Cl bond to each Cl atom).
steps: UV light supplies energy to break the Cl-Cl bond.
Homolytic fission: each Cl atom takes one electron from the bond.
Draw a curly half-arrow (fish-hook) from the bond to each Cl atom.
Products: two chlorine radicals.

questions.question: Give an equation for each of the first two propagation steps in the reaction of chlorine with butane.
questions.answer: C4H10 + Cl -> C4H9 + HCl; C4H9 + Cl2 -> C4H9Cl + Cl
steps: First propagation: a Cl radical removes an H atom from butane, giving C4H9 and HCl.
Second propagation: the C4H9 radical reacts with Cl2, giving C4H9Cl and a new Cl radical.
The Cl radical from the second step repeats the first step.

questions.question: Give the equation for a termination step that forms an alkane in the reaction of chlorine with butane.
steps: Termination joins two radicals, removing them from the chain.
Two butyl radicals (C4H9) combine.
The product is C8H18, an alkane (octane).

questions.question: Calculate the percentage yield if 1.00 g of trichlorobutane is produced from 10.0 g of butane, using C4H10 + 3Cl2 -> C4H7Cl3 + 3HCl.
steps: Moles of butane = 10.0 g / 58.0 g mol-1 = 0.172 mol.
The mole ratio butane : C4H7Cl3 is 1 : 1, so the theoretical moles of C4H7Cl3 = 0.172 mol.
M(C4H7Cl3) = 48.0 + 7.0 + 106.5 = 161.5 g mol-1, so the theoretical mass = 0.172 x 161.5 = 27.8 g.
Percentage yield = 1.00 / 27.8 x 100 = 3.59%.

questions.question: Draw the mass spectrum showing the molecular ion peaks of Cl2, given isotopic abundances of 35Cl 75% and 37Cl 25%.
questions.answer: Three peaks at m/z 70, 72 and 74 in the ratio approximately 9:6:1 (m/z 70 tallest).
steps: Possible Cl2 molecules: 35Cl-35Cl (m/z 70), 35Cl-37Cl (m/z 72), 37Cl-37Cl (m/z 74).
These are in the ratio 9 : 6 : 1.
Draw peaks at m/z 70, 72 and 74 with heights in ratio 9 : 6 : 1.

questions.question: Which type of reaction occurs when an alkane is cracked? A combustion; B hydrolysis; C neutralisation; D thermal decomposition.
steps: Cracking breaks large alkane molecules into smaller molecules using heat (and often a catalyst).
Breaking a larger molecule into smaller ones by heat is thermal decomposition.
Combustion needs oxygen and forms CO2 and H2O, which is not cracking.
Hydrolysis and neutralisation are not types of cracking.

questions.question: One molecule of a hydrocarbon is cracked to form two molecules of ethene, two molecules of propene and one molecule of propane. What is the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon? A C8H18, B C10H22, C C11H24, D C13H28.
steps: Carbon: 2 x 2 (ethene) + 2 x 3 (propene) + 3 (propane) = 13.
Hydrogen: 2 x 4 (ethene) + 2 x 6 (propene) + 8 (propane) = 28.
The hydrocarbon has 13 C and 28 H atoms.
So its formula is C13H28 (option D).

questions.question: Calculate the moles of carbon dioxide in 1.00 m3 of air at 20.0 deg C and 101 kPa, given 415 ppm of CO2 by volume (pV = nRT, R = 8.31 J mol-1 K-1).
steps: Total moles of air: n = pV/RT = (1.01 x 10^5 x 1.00)/(8.31 x 293) = 41.5 mol.
CO2 is 415 ppm by volume, which equals a mole fraction of 415 x 10^-6.

questions.question: State what is meant by complete combustion.
questions.answer: Combustion of a fuel in excess oxygen, where the only products are carbon dioxide and water.
steps: Complete combustion needs sufficient (excess) oxygen.
All carbon is fully oxidised to CO2.
All hydrogen is oxidised to H2O.
No carbon monoxide, carbon or other pollutants are formed.

questions.question: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of dodecane, C12H26, including state symbols.
steps: Carbon: 12 C gives 12 CO2.
Hydrogen: 26 H gives 13 H2O.
Oxygen on the right: 24 + 13 = 37 O atoms, so 18.5 O2 (doubling gives 2C12H26 + 37O2 -> 24CO2 + 26H2O).
Dodecane and water are liquid at room temperature; CO2 and O2 are gases.

questions.question: A jet uses 11 400 dm3 of kerosene (assumed C12H26, density 0.749 g cm-3) per hour. For a 9 hour 15 minute flight carrying 800 passengers, calculate the mass of CO2 emitted per passenger, in kg, to 3 significant figures.
questions.answer: 307 kg of CO2 per passenger (3 s.f.)
steps: Volume of fuel = 11 400 dm3/h x 9.25 h = 1.0545 x 10^5 dm3.
Mass of fuel = 1.0545 x 10^5 dm3 x 749 g dm-3 = 7.898 x 10^7 g.
Per passenger: 2.453 x 10^5 kg / 800 = 306.6 kg, so 307 kg to 3 s.f.

questions.question: Draw the skeletal formulae of the two remaining diethyloctane isomers, given the names 3,3-; 3,4-; 3,5-; and 3,6-diethyloctane.
questions.answer: 4,4-diethyloctane (both ethyl groups on C4) and 4,5-diethyloctane (one ethyl on C4 and one on C5).
steps: Number the octane chain C1 to C8; ethyl groups must sit on C3 to C6 to keep octane as the longest chain.
The possible pairs are 3,3; 3,4; 3,5; 3,6; 4,4; 4,5 (others are mirror images of these).
The two not yet drawn are 4,4 and 4,5.
Draw an eight-carbon chain with two ethyl (CH2CH3) branches on C4 (4,4) and on C4 and C5 (4,5).

questions.question: How many hydrogen atoms are in 14 g of methane? [L = 6.02 x 10^23] A 5.268 x 10^23; B 6.880 x 10^23; C 2.107 x 10^24; D 2.752 x 10^24.
steps: Moles of CH4 = 14 g / 16.0 g mol-1 = 0.875 mol.
Each CH4 has 4 H atoms, so H atoms = 4 x 0.875 = 3.5 mol.
Number of H atoms = 3.5 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 2.107 x 10^24.
